title: Pleated Shorts Sewing Pattern – Free PDF
content:
Garment High waisted pleated shorts with a fly zipper

Level Intermediate

Sizes US 00 – 22 (XXS – 4XL)

Fabric Linen, cotton twill, chambray, light denim or soft suiting

Pieces 7

This free pleated shorts sewing pattern makes tailored, high waisted shorts with two soft pleats on each front, slanted side pockets, a real fly zipper and a straight buttoned waistband. The legs are short and straight, so the shorts look sharp with a tucked-in shirt and relaxed with a simple tee.

→ Jump to the free download

1 cm (3/8″) seam allowance included on all pieces · 2 cm (3/4″) hem on the legs · trouser zipper 18 cm (7″) for sizes 00–0, 23 cm (9″) for 2–22 · 1 button

Design details of the pleated shorts

Each front has two pleats folded toward the centre front and stitched only into the waistband, so they open softly below and give room at the hip without bulk. The slanted pockets have a main-fabric pocket bag, so the fabric you see through the opening matches the shorts, and each back has one waist dart for a smooth fit over the seat.

Reading the sketch

On the front, the short curved lines under the waistband are the two pleats on each side, and the long diagonal lines from the waistband to the sides are the slanted pocket openings. The J-shaped line next to the centre is the fly topstitching, and the small circle on the waistband is the button.

On the back, the line in the middle is the centre back seam and the two short lines from the waistband are the darts. The small cross lines near the hem only show the leg shape; the hem itself is plain, with no cuffs.

  • Straight 3 cm (1 1/4″) waistband with one button and a 3 cm underlap extension
  • Front fly zipper with curved topstitching and a fly shield behind it
  • Two pleats on each front, folded toward the centre front
  • Slanted side pockets with a main-fabric pocket bag and a lining
  • One waist dart on each back and a centre back seam
  • Short straight legs, about 34 cm (13 3/8″) long in size 8, with a 2 cm (3/4″) hem
  • No belt loops, no back pockets and no elastic

They are the kind of shorts you wear every summer, and a good first fly zipper project: everything else is simple, so you can take your time on the fly. If you like the pleated look, the same details work in a longer leg.

Sizing guide

Measure your natural waist and your hips, and choose the size by your waist: the waistband is fitted, while the pleats give room at the hip. Not sure how to measure? See how to take body measurements and how to choose your sewing pattern size.

US sizes 00 to 22, drafted for a height of 167.75 cm (5 ft 6 in). Letter sizes are a guide only: 00 = XXS · 0–2 = XS · 4–6 = S · 8–10 = M · 12–14 = L · 16 = XL · 18 = 2XL · 20 = 3XL · 22 = 4XL. Always choose by measurements.

Body measurements

Finished shorts measurements

The waistband has about 1.5 cm (5/8″) of ease. The two pleats on each front add 9 to 14 cm (3 1/2 to 5 1/2″) of extra room at the hip. Rises are measured without the waistband; the leg opening is the full width around one leg.

Fabric amounts

Estimated with every piece laid out for each size, plus about 8 %. The waistband is cut in one long strip along the grain, so it sets the length; the interfacing for it can be joined from two pieces. Buy a little more for a one-way print and pre-wash the fabric.

Common fit adjustments

Length. The shorts end at the upper thigh. Add the same amount at the hem of the front and back for a longer leg, or a Bermuda length. Full guide: how to lengthen or shorten a sewing pattern.

Waist and hips. If your hips are bigger than the size chosen by your waist, blend between sizes on the side seams of the front, back and pocket bag, from the waist size at the top to the hip size lower down.

Materials

  • Main fabric: 0.9 to 1.3 m (1 to 1 1/2 yd) of a light to medium-weight woven
  • Pocket lining: 0.4 m (1/2 yd) of cotton poplin, lawn or pocketing
  • Interfacing: medium-weight fusible interfacing for the waistband and the fly
  • Zipper: one trouser zipper, 18 cm (7″) for sizes 00–0 or 23 cm (9″) for sizes 2–22
  • Button: one 1 cm (3/8″) button for the waistband
  • Matching thread, zipper foot, optional stay tape for the pocket openings

Pattern pieces

  • 1 Pants Front: cut 2 (with the fly extension)
  • 2 Pants Back: cut 2
  • 3 Waistband: cut 1 + 1 in interfacing (drawn whole)
  • 4 Pocket Bag: cut 2 in main fabric
  • 5 Fly Facing: cut 1
  • 6 Pocket Lining: cut 2 in lining
  • 7 Fly Interfacing: cut 1 in interfacing

Choosing fabric for pleated shorts

Pleated shorts need a woven with a little body, so the pleats hang neatly and the fly lies flat. Linen and linen blends are the classic summer choice, cotton twill or chino gives a crisp everyday pair, and chambray or a light denim up to 8 oz works well too. A soft suiting or crepe, like the small check of our olive version, makes them smart enough for the office.

Avoid very drapey fabrics like rayon challis, which make the pleats collapse, and very stiff denim, which is hard to sew at the fly. More tips in how to choose fabric for sewing patterns and how to use fusible interfacing.

Sewing notes

Fit and style

A fitted waistband with about 1.5 cm of ease and roomy pleats below. Baste the side seams and try the shorts on before the waistband.

Fabric

Light to medium-weight wovens with some body. Press the pleats only at the top for a soft drape, or all the way down for a sharp look.

Fly zipper

The trickiest step. Mark the fold lines, baste the centre front first and follow the pictures slowly. See how to sew a zipper.

Get the pattern

Free PDF pattern, one file per size, US sizes 00 to 22 (XXS to 4XL). Share your make with #sewcraftly!

Download A4
Download US Letter

Print page 1 at 100% and check that the test square measures 10 cm (4 in). New to PDF patterns? Read how to print and assemble a PDF pattern.

Sewing steps

Seam allowance 1 cm (3/8″) unless stated otherwise. Sew right sides together and press every seam before it is crossed by another one. Left and right always mean as worn.

  1. Prepare. Transfer all markings. Fuse interfacing to the waistband, and the Fly Interfacing to the fly extension of the right front. Finish the side seams, inseams and front crotch edges of all four leg pieces.
  2. Pleats and darts. On each front, fold the two pleats toward the centre front following the arrows and baste them across the waistline. Sew the waist dart on each back and press it toward the centre back.
  3. Slanted pockets. Sew the Pocket Lining to the slanted edge of each front, trim and understitch, then turn it inside. Place the Pocket Bag under it, sew the two pocket layers together around the bottom and baste the pocket to the front at the waist and side.
  4. Fly zipper. Sew the fronts together at the crotch up to the circle and baste the fly opening closed. Sew the zipper to the left extension, then to the right extension, and topstitch the curved fly line from the right side. Add the folded Fly Facing behind the zipper on the left and bar-tack the bottom of the fly.
  5. Inseams. Sew each front to its back at the short inseam and press open.
  6. Crotch seam. Sew the rest of the crotch seam from the back waist to the front, reinforce the curve with a second row of stitching and finish the seam allowances together.
  7. Side seams. Sew the side seams, catching the pocket bags, and press them open.
  8. Waistband. Press under one long edge of the waistband, sew the other edge to the waist with the button extension on the left front, close the ends, turn and slipstitch or stitch in the ditch. Make the buttonhole and sew on the button.
  9. Hem. Finish the lower edges, turn up 2 cm (3/4″) and stitch by machine or with a blind hem. Give the shorts a final press.

Tips and common mistakes

Pleats that point the wrong way. Mark both lines of each pleat on the right side and always fold in the direction of the arrow, toward the centre front, so all four pleats match.

Stretched pocket openings. The slanted edge is cut on the bias and stretches easily. Press a strip of stay tape or interfacing along it before sewing the lining, and understitch.

A fly that gapes. Baste the centre front closed before sewing the zipper and remove the basting only at the end. Topstitch the curve slowly, with the zipper pull moved out of the way.

A waistband that is too tight. With only 1.5 cm of ease, try the shorts on before sewing the waistband and adjust the side seams if needed.

How to style pleated shorts

City: in a check suiting or a crisp cotton twill with a tucked-in shirt, loafers and a thin belt over the waistband.

Summer: in linen with a tank top and sandals. For an even easier summer make, try our free high waisted biker shorts sewing pattern.

All year: love the pleats? Our free barrel pants sewing pattern has the same relaxed, pleated front in a full-length leg.

Care

Wash according to your fabric, inside out, with the zipper closed. Press the pleats from the wrong side or through a pressing cloth, especially on linen, wool blends and dark colours.

Questions

Is seam allowance included?

Yes: 1 cm (3/8″) on every seam, and a 2 cm (3/4″) hem on both legs.

Which paper sizes are included?

The free download has A4 and US Letter files, one file per size, so you only print the size you need.

Which size should I choose?

Choose by your waist measurement: the waistband is fitted, with only about 1.5 cm (5/8″) of ease. The two pleats on each front give plenty of room at the hip. If your hips are more than one size bigger than your waist, blend between sizes at the side seams.

Do I need belt loops or a belt?

No. The straight 3 cm (1 1/4″) waistband closes with one button and an underlap, and there are no belt loops, so the waist stays clean and neat.

Which zipper do I need?

A trouser or jeans zipper (metal or nylon): 18 cm (7″) for sizes 00 and 0, 23 cm (9″) for sizes 2 to 22. A longer zipper is easy to shorten, the steps explain how.

Are these pleated shorts hard to sew?

They are an intermediate project. The pleats, darts and pockets are easy; the fly zipper is the only tricky part, and the steps take you through it slowly.

Can I make them longer?

Yes. The pattern is drafted for a height of 167.75 cm (5 ft 6 in) and ends at the upper thigh. The leg is straight, so you can add length at the hem of the front and back for a Bermuda length.
